title: Cloud channel entry creative brief & onramp scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
A lightweight creative + technical checklist to get Redwood listed in a cloud catalog (AWS/Azure/GCP style) via our channel partners. This document is a scratchpad — rough copy, acceptance gates, and a minimal telemetry/entitlement checklist for engineering and GTM to align on a fast, low-friction onramp.

Context / constraints (quick):
- This is for the "bring-your-own-tenant" public listing flow (no private VPC install via the marketplace).
- We need a tile for cloud catalog, entitlements mapping, SKU for trial/paid, and a short onboarding script for partner sellers.
- Security/compliance blurb must call out data-in-transit, KMS support, and optional Private deployment link for enterprise customers.

High-level acceptance criteria (must pass before submit):
1) Copy approved by marketing + legal: short, medium, long variants exist.
2) SKU mapping complete with trial flow and meter dimensions approved by finance.
3) Minimal integration tests: provisioning webhook, entitlement callback, event telemetry visible in Console.
4) Security checklist: TLS certs, KMS integration docs linked, SSO note for enterprise.

Tile copy (short snippets to A/B test)
- Tile title (<= 50 chars): "Redwood Inference: Fast, predictable LLM inference"
- Subtitle (<= 90 chars): "Low-latency text generation, embeddings, and model routing — hosted or dedicated"
- One-liner (hero line): "Run LLM inference at production scale with predictable latency and cost controls."

Key benefit bullets (3–5, 80 char max each):
- Predictable latency and dedicated capacity options for production apps
- Cost controls: batching, cache, and quantization recommendations
- Unified API across hosted, reserved, and private deployments
- Rollout tools: canary, A/B, and automatic fallbacks for reliability

Medium description (~2–3 short paragraphs)
- Paragraph 1: What it is
  Redwood Inference is a developer-first runtime that makes serving large language models simple and production-ready. Integrate via a single API to access text generation, chat, embeddings, and reranking backed by optimized GPU serving.
- Paragraph 2: Why it matters
  Ship faster with predictable performance and lower operational overhead — choose hosted inference for fast time-to-value, reserved capacity for throughput guarantees, or private deployment for regulated workloads.
- Paragraph 3: Quickstart
  Sign up, select a model from our curated catalog, and start generating using a single REST call. Sample requests and SDK snippets provided in the onboarding guide.

Long description / support copy (for listing detail page)
- Include: compliance summary (SOC2, ISO if applicable), region availability, support SLAs for Dedicated customers, and pointer to pricing matrix.
- Technical links: onboarding guide URL, API reference, billing SKU table, telemetry events doc (see below).

CTA variants to test
- "Start free — 30k tokens"
- "Try a hosted demo"
- "Request Dedicated capacity"
- "Contact sales for Private deployment"

SKU & entitlements (draft)
- Offer types: free-trial, pay-as-you-go, reserved-monthly
- SKU example (human-readable): RW-INF-HOSTED-TRIAL, RW-INF-PAYG-TOKEN, RW-INF-DEDICATED-MONTHLY
- Metering dims: tokens_generated, embeddings_units, dedicated_hours
- Trial gating: 30k token quota, expires after 30 days OR conversion to PAYG on card

Integration checklist (engineers)
- Pre-submit:
  - [ ] Provisioning webhook (catalog -> Redwood) endpoint implemented and testable
  - [ ] Entitlement sync API (pull/push) for tenant activation done
  - [ ] Billing webhook to map SKU->internal plan (test event present)
  - [ ] Telemetry events emitted and visible in internal Console dashboard (see event names)
  - [ ] Sample quickstart snippet included in package

Telemetry (minimal required events for listing)
- event: market_onboard.requested -> payload includes partner_id, tenant_id, sku_id
- event: market_onboard.activated -> payload includes tenant_id, plan, trial_end_ts
- event: billing.usage.reported -> tokens, embeddings_units, timestamp
- event: market_onboard.error -> code, message, mitigations

Ops + SRE notes
- SLA considerations: for Dedicated SKUs we must surface latency SLO and incident contact for partners (TBD exact page)
- Rollback logic: catalog worst-case rollback -> revoke entitlements + notify tenant owners

Legal & compliance (notes to legal)
- Need copy for: data residency, PII handling, optional private deployment add-on (legal language), indemnity for third-party marketplace terms
- Confirm whether listing requires additional security attestation doc upload (some clouds require compliance package)

Outstanding questions / blockers
- Who will own the marketplace support queue post-launch? (GTM or Solutions Eng?)
- Do we want a demo tenant pre-provisioned for partners to try in-situ? (Pros: easy demo; Cons: staleness)
- Marketplace listing meta: do we need additional screenshots (Console, latency graphs) or just 1 hero screenshot?

Sample onboarding script for partner sellers (30–60s elevator)
"Redwood Inference gives your customers consistent LLM inference with predictable latency and costs across hosted and private deployments. Sign them up from the catalog, grant a 30k token trial, and they can test latency and output quality within minutes. For enterprise needs we offer dedicated GPUs and on-prem options — we’ll handle the rollout and SLAs."

Quick test plan (pre-launch)
- Manual smoke: provision via catalog UI -> confirm tenant active -> run sample generation -> check telemetry
- Automated e2e: provisioning webhook + entitlement + billing event -> simulate usage -> validate metrics and invoice mapping

Next steps (owner + ETA)
- Aisha: finalize short/medium/long copy and submit to legal for quick review (ETA 2024-11-12)
- Daniel: stub provisioning webhook and instrument market_onboard events (ETA 2024-11-19)
- Sofia: draft tile image concepts and hero screenshot variants (ETA 2024-11-18)
- Owen: coordinate SKU mapping with finance and get sample billing events (ETA 2024-11-20)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep copy lean — catalog tiles get scanned quickly. Emphasize "predictable performance" not just speed.
- Avoid deep technical jargon on the tile. Put the heavy details on the listing detail page.
- We may want an "enterprise" filter tag on the catalog to surface Dedicated/Private options separately.

Links & references (quick):
- Internal API spec: confluence:cloud-catalog-integration-spec
- Billing mapping doc: JIRA-3421
- Dev PR: GH-PR-1187

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Finalize copy A/B variants
- [ ] Attach hero screenshot mockups
- [ ] Confirm legal compliance upload requirements
- [ ] Run e2e smoke and record results

End of scratchpad. Keep edits short and iterative — this is the working source for the channel listing deliverable.
